title: How many objects does new String("abc") create?
context: How many String objects are created by `String s1 = new String("abc");`?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Usually two. The literal "abc" is placed in the String constant pool, which is one object, if it is not already there. `new String(...)` then creates a second object on the heap that copies the characters. The variable points to the heap object, so `s1 == "abc"` is false. If "abc" was already in the pool, only the heap object is new. Calling `intern()` returns the pooled object.

points.title: Literal plus heap copy
points.why: The literal goes to the pool and new String creates a separate heap object.

points.title: Reference comparison
points.why: The variable refers to the heap copy, so == against the literal is false.
